clue.text: Speaks about a son and daughter's carefree youth

indicators.note: the verb for speaking wraps itself around the other pieces, as about can mean surrounding

parts.note: speaks means says
a son is a lad

explanation.surface: Someone talks fondly about a son and daughter enjoying their untroubled childhood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' wraps the speaking word around the rest, so it splits after its first letter rather than at its ends.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom, from Shakespeare, means the innocent, untroubled period of one's early life.

clue.text: Strong second row

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for second, as a unit of time
a row (rhyming with cow) is a quarrel or tiff

explanation.surface: Reads like a sports report praising a powerful second row in a rugby scrum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' looks like a line of players, but it is the argument sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A drink or wind can be described as stiff when it is potent or forceful.

clue.text: Record in online diary, not book

indicators.note: not means the letter for book is left out of the diary word

parts.note: a blog is an online diary

explanation.surface: Someone notes something in a web diary rather than a printed one.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship's log is a written record kept of events, so to record is to enter in one.

clue.text: Wife and powerful businessman disposing of old farm building

parts.note: 'my old Dutch' is Cockney slang for one's wife

indicators.note: disposing of tells us the abbreviation for old is thrown out of the magnate word

parts.note: a baron is a powerful business magnate, as in press baron

explanation.surface: A wife and a tycoon getting rid of an outdated barn on their land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'My old Dutch' is London Cockney slang for a wife, from 'Duchess of Fife'. Deleting O from BARON leaves BARN.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a roofed open-sided structure for storing hay on agricultural land.

clue.text: Son entering stadium with large magazine

indicators.note: entering means the letter for son goes inside the stadium word

parts.note: an arena is a stadium
L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: A boy walks into a football ground carrying a large magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Magazine' suggests a publication, and Arsenal is also a London football club, but here it is a store of weapons.
explanation.definitionFit: A magazine in its military sense is a store for arms and ammunition, which is what an arsenal is.

clue.text: Drink, more bubbly, for boss

parts.note: to sup is to drink

indicators.note: bubbly suggests fizzing and churning, so the word more is mixed up

explanation.surface: An order for a drink and more champagne for the boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bubbly' looks like champagne, but it is the anagram signal turning MORE into REMO.
explanation.definitionFit: A supremo is the person in overall charge of an organisation, its chief.

clue.text: Stage favourites returned

indicators.note: returned means the word for favourites is read backwards

parts.note: a teacher's pets are favourites

explanation.surface: Popular performers coming back to the theatre stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stage' suggests a theatre, but it means a phase or step in a process.
explanation.definitionFit: A stage in a process is one phase of progress, a synonym in that sense.

clue.text: Verger — traumatic death he suffers — a case for Miss Marple

indicators.note: suffers suggests the words are knocked about and broken up, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A church official comes to a traumatic end, the very situation of an Agatha Christie whodunit.
explanation.walkthrough: All 22 letters of VERGER TRAUMATIC DEATH HE are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Agatha Christie's 1930 novel was the first full-length mystery solved by her elderly sleuth.

clue.text: Gradually, bishop, for one, imposed on me, a student

indicators.note: in a down clue, one part placed on top of another comes first

parts.note: a bishop is one example of a chess piece
L, for learner, stands for a student

explanation.surface: A bishop gradually imposes himself on a student and me.
explanation.definitionFit: Done piecemeal means done bit by bit, a little at a time.

clue.text: Piece of music filed away by librarian

indicators.note: filed away by suggests something tucked inside the word, so the answer sits within its letters

explanation.surface: A librarian files away a piece of sheet music.
explanation.definitionFit: An aria is a solo song in an opera or oratorio, so a musical piece.

clue.text: At work, bought bar of gold?

parts.note: someone at work is in, present at their job
to have got something is to have obtained it, as by buying

explanation.surface: Someone at work boasting of having bought a gold bar.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks gold as one example: such a bar may be silver too.
explanation.definitionFit: Precious metal cast into a block for storage is called an ingot.

clue.text: Replace marvellous watch set with diamonds

parts.note: super means marvellous

indicators.note: set with suggests something embedded in a mount, so the diamonds letter goes inside the watching word

parts.note: to watch is to see
D is the abbreviation for diamonds, the card suit

explanation.surface: Swapping a fine watch for one encrusted with diamonds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Watch' looks like a timepiece and 'set with diamonds' like jewellery, but watch is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To supersede something is to take its place, ousting it.

clue.text: Large fortune? There's no hope of that!

parts.note: fat means large
chance means fortune or luck

explanation.surface: Someone dreams of a huge fortune and is told it will never happen.
explanation.definitionFit: The ironic idiom is a scornful way of saying something is very unlikely.

clue.text: See 7
A pleasantly appealing accent

parts.note: cute means attractive in a pleasing way

explanation.surface: Someone describes a charming way of speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Accent' suggests a way of speaking, but it is the mark over a letter, as in é.
explanation.definitionFit: The acute is a diacritic mark slanting upwards to the right, one kind of written accent.

clue.text: Win 'EV' appearing in April (tricky)

indicators.note: appearing in means the two letters show up inside the other word
tricky suggests something awkward and twisted, so the month's letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Something called 'EV' turning up in a difficult April and winning.
explanation.walkthrough: The quoted 'EV' looks like a code to decode but is used literally; 'tricky' scrambles the month into PRAIL, which 'appearing in' wraps round it.
explanation.definitionFit: To prevail is to triumph, to come out on top.

clue.text: Quickly sat with those working under pressure

indicators.note: in a down clue the reworked letters sit under the pressure letter

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for pressure in physics

indicators.note: working suggests the letters are being worked over and reshaped into a new order

explanation.surface: People quickly sat down with colleagues working under pressure.
explanation.definitionFit: The old adverb means with great speed, as fast as possible.

clue.text: Late extra expected

parts.note: over can mean extra or left over, as in surplus
due means expected, as in the train is due

explanation.surface: An extra item is late though expected.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that has not arrived by the time it was expected is behind schedule.

clue.text: Last of those (Labour) to make a speech in complex

indicators.note: last of means only the final letter of the word those is taken

parts.note: Lab is the abbreviation for the British Labour Party
to orate is to make a speech

explanation.surface: The last Labour politicians to speak in some complicated debate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Complex' looks like a noun such as a building complex, but it is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Elaborate means intricate and detailed, with many parts.

clue.text: Top shop gutted close to the centre

indicators.note: gutted means the insides are removed, leaving only the outside letters of shop

parts.note: inner means near the middle

explanation.surface: A top shop has been gutted near the town centre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top' looks like an adjective, but it is the child's toy that twirls on its point.
explanation.definitionFit: A spinning top is a toy that whirls round on its point.

clue.text: Take back tense former US president from the south

indicators.note: in a down clue, reading from the south means from the bottom upwards

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for tense in grammar
Jimmy Carter was a former US president

explanation.surface: A tense ex-president of the United States, from the southern states, takes something back.
explanation.walkthrough: Carter came from Georgia, so 'from the south' plays on his origins.
explanation.definitionFit: To retract a statement is to withdraw it, admitting it should not have been said.

clue.text: Question a ruler abroad causing controversy

indicators.note: abroad can mean all over the place, astray, so the letters are scattered

explanation.surface: Someone questions a foreign ruler, stirring up a dispute.
explanation.definitionFit: A quarrel is an argument or dispute, a heated disagreement.

clue.text: I agree to leave ahead of English, therefore

indicators.note: ahead of puts the leaving word before the letter for English

parts.note: to quit is to leave
so means therefore

explanation.surface: Someone agrees to leave before the English do.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a mildly formal expression of agreement, like 'exactly'.

clue.text: Try leader of team, in essence

parts.note: a judge hears or tries a case in court

indicators.note: leader of means the first letter of team

explanation.surface: An encouraging word to try harder for the team captain, at heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Try' looks like effort or a rugby score, but it is a court trying a case.
explanation.definitionFit: The heart of a matter is its core or most essential part.

clue.text: Row in match on river

parts.note: a tie is a match, as in a cup tie

explanation.surface: A spectator in a row of seats at a riverside match.
explanation.walkthrough: A cup tie is the British term for a knockout football match.
explanation.definitionFit: A tier is one of a series of rows set one above another, as in a stadium.

clue.text: Balding, with obsession mostly about cap

indicators.note: mostly means the last letter of the obsession word is dropped

parts.note: having a thing about something is an obsession
on means about, concerning
a cap is a top, as on a bottle

explanation.surface: Someone losing their hair is obsessive about their cap.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone whose hair is sparse on the crown, losing it.

clue.text: Baffling question for model

definitions.meaning: a puzzling problem that is hard to answer
someone who strikes attitudes for a photographer or artist

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a puzzle and one who sits or stands posed for a picture.

clue.text: Old friend gets draw

parts.note: stale means old and no longer fresh
a mate is a friend

explanation.surface: An old pal draws a picture, or ties a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Draw' looks like a verb, but it is the result of a chess game ending level.
explanation.definitionFit: In chess, this position ends the game with neither side winning, so it is a drawn result.

clue.text: In which one will find this mountain range?

definitions.text: In which one will find this mountain range?

parts.words: In which one will find this mountain range?
parts.note: the book of maps where one looks up ranges shares its name with the North African mountains

explanation.surface: A question asking where one might locate a mountain range.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer works twice: the reference book with maps of the world, and the North African mountain range of the same name.
explanation.definitionFit: A bound book of maps would show mountain ranges, including the one in Morocco with this name.

clue.text: Permit carried by couple touring

indicators.note: carried by means the answer is held inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Permission carried by a couple who are going on tour.
explanation.definitionFit: To let someone do something is to allow it.

clue.text: Big occasion, not finished yet

indicators.note: not finished means the last letter of the occasion word is cut off

parts.note: an event is a big occasion

explanation.surface: A big occasion that is still not over yet.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words intensify a comparison, as in 'even better' or 'yet better'.

clue.text: Forced to wear set in sports car, perhaps

indicators.note: forced suggests the letters are pushed out of shape and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone forced to put on a set outfit, in a sports car perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: A vehicle with room for just a driver and one passenger; many sports cars are like that.
